pointers.sentence: `response_for_exception` passes any exception it does not recognise to `handle_uncaught_exception`, which returns what `technical_500_response` makes unless `settings.DEBUG_PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS` is on, and it calls the same function directly, with a status of 400, for a `BadRequest` or a `SuspiciousOperation` ([How an exception becomes a response](../handlers/exceptions.md)) (`django/core/handlers/exception.py:response_for_exception`).

The logging system asks, and under Django's default logging configuration only when `settings.DEBUG` is off: the configuration gives the logger `"django"` an `AdminEmailHandler` for records of level ERROR and above, behind a filter that passes them only while the setting is off ([Logging](../startup/logging.md#adminemailhandler-error-email-is-a-log-handler)) (`django/utils/log.py:DEFAULT_LOGGING`).

For each record it mails, the handler makes a reporter as for an email, with `is_email=True`, puts the text report in the message, and adds the HTML report as an alternative body if it was made with `include_html=True` (`django/utils/log.py:AdminEmailHandler.emit`).

With `settings.DEBUG` off, `ADMINS` set, and `MAILERS`, the setting that names a project's mail backends, set to one that keeps each message in memory, a request for the Gazette's failing view shows the mail made inside the logging call (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`, `django/core/mail/backends/locmem.py:EmailBackend`).

With `settings.DEBUG` off, `ADMINS` set, and `MAILERS`, the setting that names a project's mail backends, set to one that keeps each message in memory, a request for the Gazette's failing view shows the mail made inside the logging call (`django/core/mail/handler.py:MailersHandler.create_connection`, `django/core/mail/backends/locmem.py:EmailBackend`).
It makes a reporter, asks it for one of two renderings, and wraps the result in a response with the status it was given (`django/views/debug.py:technical_500_response`).
So a project can replace the reporter for the whole site, and a middleware can replace it for one request's debug page (`django/views/debug.py:get_exception_reporter_class`).

An empty policy means that `ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware` adds no header, so the debug page is exempt from the site's Content Security Policy (`django/middleware/csp.py:ContentSecurityPolicyMiddleware.process_response`).
`ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_data` turns them into one dictionary, which is the context for both templates (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_data`).

It collects the whole chain, stopping with a warning if the chain loops back on itself, and then reports the frames oldest exception first (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_frames`).

And there is a type, `"django"` for a frame whose module's name begins with `django.` and `"user"` for any other, which the HTML page puts on the frame as a class, so that the two can be styled apart (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter.get_exception_traceback_frames`).

The address is built without the usual validation of the `"Host"` header: a request with a host the site does not allow would raise if asked for its host in the ordinary way ([Headers, host and scheme](../http/headers.md)) (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter._get_raw_insecure_uri`).
The user is included as text, inside a `try`, since asking for the user can itself fail when the database is the thing that is down (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_data`).

`ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_html` and `ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_text` render the dictionary with `django/views/templates/technical_500.html` and `django/views/templates/technical_500.txt`.

`ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_html` and `ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_text` render the dictionary with `django/views/templates/technical_500.html` and `django/views/templates/technical_500.txt`.
At each call the reporter opens the file itself and gives the text to `DEBUG_ENGINE`, an `Engine` made in this module for nothing else (`django/views/debug.py:ExceptionReporter.get_traceback_html`).

The error templates have an engine of their own so that they render however the project has set `TEMPLATES`, and they are read from the filesystem directly, in the words of the comment above `DEBUG_ENGINE`, "so that the error handler works even if the template loader is broken" (`django/views/debug.py:DEBUG_ENGINE`).
A reporter made for an email also leaves out of the HTML the source lines around each frame, and the page's script (`django/views/templates/technical_500.html`).
It makes no reporter: it shows what the resolver tried (`django/views/debug.py:technical_404_response`).
